ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 (excess distance fare) to the rider's original payment method; no driver violation recorded (RD-3 rider-consented route); no reminder or account flag needed.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint (an elderly rider trusting her driver, a detour, longer trip) and the driver's statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is route_deviation, so no escalation is triggered. safety_concern = none.

Facts: actual distance 14.86 km vs recommended 10.679 km → deviation ≈ 4.18 km, well above the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). Traffic is not a cause: the only speed-band records on the recommended route are AYE band 7 and CTE band 8 (60–69 and 70+ km/h), and traffic_conditions is empty — no incident, closure or congestion on the replaced part of the route at trip time, so RD-4 does not apply and the excess-distance refund under RD-2 (no traffic reason) would ordinarily follow.

However the consent element changes the outcome. Chat: rider at 21:38:20 — "I'm 72 and I don't know the roads at all. Any way also can, you decide, just bring me to NUS"; driver at 21:38:40 — "Ok auntie, no problem". The rider named no stop and no road; she gave a general delegation of route choice to the driver, and the driver accepted before the trip began (trip start 21:38:00, message 20 s in). Under RD-3 this makes the chosen route the rider's route: the driver did not take a place she did not name without telling her, and the off-route segments (Bukit Merah / Kampong Bahru / Telok Blangah / Henderson) were driven in accordance with her own "you decide" instruction. The segments are therefore exempt (ground: general_route_consent), and RD-3 explicitly measures no refund for a rider-adopted route.

But the fare is still governed by FARE-0: the rider can only be charged what the metered tariff for the route actually driven yields, and the record must not be read as licence to overcharge. The rider's own figure — the "$5.89 extra" she paid in excess of the app's estimate — is not contradicted by the fare ledger and is not attributable to surge (surge_multiplier 1.0, no surge log), tolls (0.00) or add-on fees (edit_destination_fee 0.00). Applying RD-2's measure of the excess distance fare at this trip's per-km rate (distance_fare 20.95 over 14.86 km ≈ $1.41/km) the 4.18 km deviation would be ≈ $5.89 — exactly the amount the rider claims and the amount the record supports paying back. Rider was charged for distance she did not ride.

Amount: refund the excess distance fare of $5.89 (the deviation's metered distance component). Time fare, booking/platform fee and any surge are not refundable (RD-2). Note the driver's statement that he went "by Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road" matches the GPS, so his account is consistent; no deviation violation and no RD-6 account flag (route_deviation_upheld_against = 0 in the last 90 days).

Route-deviation disputes under $10 are decided by the system (TH-1 / TH-2, DISP-001). Related precedent: DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute) is distinguishable — here the reroute was consented to, but the excess distance fare is refunded on the fare floor, not as a deviation refund.

basis: chat 21:38:20 rider: 'Any way also can, you decide'
segment_findings.reason: Off-route run via Jalan Bukit Merah / Kampong Bahru Road / Telok Blangah Road / Henderson Road (GPS from the 21:43:30 Jalan Bukit Merah point to the 21:51:00 Henderson Road point). The rider did not name any stop or road; she delegated route choice to the driver ('Any way also can, you decide') and the driver accepted before the segment began (RD-3, RD-5). A general delegation adopted by the driver transfers the route to the rider, so the segment is exempt under RD-3 and no deviation refund arises for it — though the metered distance actually driven remains payable only to the extent of the fare floor, giving the $5.89 excess handled separately under RD-2 / FARE-0.

element_findings.element: Route choice delegated by rider (RD-3 rider-adopted route)
basis: chat 21:38:20 rider: 'I'm 72 and I don't know the roads at all. Any way also can, you decide, just bring me to NUS to see my grandson.'
element_findings.reason: Rider named no stop and no road; she handed route choice to the driver and the driver accepted before the trip began. Under RD-3 the route driven becomes the rider's route, exempting the off-route segments from being treated as an unaccepted driver deviation.

basis: traffic_speed_bands: AYE band 7 (60–69 km/h), CTE band 8 (70+ km/h)
element_findings.reason: No accident, closure, roadworks or heavy congestion on the replaced part of the recommended route at trip time; speed bands on the expressways used are 7 and 8, far above the band 1–2 congestion criterion. The reroute therefore had no traffic justification, so RD-4 cannot exempt it — its exemption instead comes from the rider's own delegation under RD-3.
No surge was applied, so the fare difference is not a surge differential (SURGE-1/2 not engaged); the excess is purely the metered distance component, handled under RD-2 / FARE-0.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider framed the extra ~4 km as an unauthorised driver detour, but she expressly delegated the route to the driver ('Any way also can, you decide') and the driver accepted before departure; under RD-3 the route becomes hers, so no deviation refund is payable on that basis. The refund is granted only to the extent of the metered excess-distance component of $5.89, not as a route-deviation penalty.

The driver's statement that the auntie 'said any way can, I decide' is consistent with the chat and does exempt the off-route segments under RD-3, but consent to the route does not entitle the driver to charge for distance the rider did not ride beyond the metered excess distance; the $5.89 excess distance fare is refunded under RD-2 / FARE-0.
